title: Actions in ASP.NET Core
description: Learn about action methods, their return types, and how to pass data from controllers to views.

data.text: What Is an Action Method?

An **action method** is a public method inside a controller class. When a user visits a URL, ASP.NET Core's routing system finds the matching controller and calls the corresponding action method. The action method performs its work — fetching data, processing a form, or running a calculation — and then returns a response.

terms.definition: A public method on a controller class that handles an HTTP request and returns a response.
An abstract class that represents the result of an action method, such as a view, JSON, or a redirect.
An interface implemented by all action results. It is the most common return type for action methods because it allows returning different result types from the same method.

data.caption: How a browser request flows through a controller action to a view.

data.text: Action Method Basics
Every action method is a `public` method that returns `IActionResult` (or a more specific type). The simplest action method just returns a view:

data.title: Minimal action method
data.content: A simple action that returns a view.

data.text: The method name (`Index`) is the action name. When the URL `/Home/Index` is requested, routing calls this method. The `return View()` line tells ASP.NET Core to find and render the corresponding Razor view (`Views/Home/Index.cshtml`).
Common Action Return Types
Action methods can return many different types. Here are the most common ones you will use as a beginner:

rows: Showing a page to the user
Returns a raw HTTP status code
Sending the user to another URL

data.title: Beginner Tip
data.text: Stick with `IActionResult` as your return type while learning. It is flexible enough to return views, JSON, or redirects from the same method without changing the signature.
Returning Models to Views
Action methods often need to send data to a view. There are two main ways to do this: passing a simple type (like a string or number) or passing a class instance (a model).
Returning a Simple Type
You can return a simple string or number by casting it to `object` when passing it to the `View()` method:

data.text: In the corresponding view, declare the model as `@model string` and display it with `@Model`.
Returning a Class Model
For more complex data, create a C# class and return an instance of it:

data.content: A simple model class representing an employee.

data.text: The view then declares `@model Employee` and can access each property through `@Model.Name`, `@Model.Salary`, and so on.
ViewResult Overloads
The `View()` helper method has several overloads (versions) that accept different arguments:

items: `View()` — renders the default view for this action.
`View("Detail")` — renders a specific view by name.
`View(model)` — renders the default view with a model.
`View("Detail", model)` — renders a named view with a model.

data.text: Transferring Data Without a Model
Sometimes you need to pass small amounts of data without creating a full model class. ASP.NET Core gives you three tools for this: ViewBag, ViewData, and TempData.

cards.title: ViewBag
cards.description: A dynamic object that lets you assign properties at runtime.

cards.title: ViewData
cards.description: A dictionary of objects accessed by string keys.

cards.title: TempData
cards.description: A dictionary that survives a single redirect using session state.
cons: Value is removed after it is read

data.text: Using TempData for Redirects
When you redirect to another action, ViewBag values are lost. Use TempData instead. It stores values in session state so they survive one redirect:

data.title: Remember
data.text: TempData values are automatically removed after they are read. Call `TempData.Keep()` if you need to read them again without losing them.
Session Variables
Session state persists data across all requests from the same user until the session expires. It requires two additions to `Program.cs`:

items: Add `app.UseSession()` in the middleware pipeline before `app.MapControllerRoute()`.

data.text: Session state uses server memory by default. For large-scale apps, consider distributed cache providers like Redis instead.
Redirections
Action methods can redirect users to another URL or another action. Each redirect method returns a specific result type:

rows: Temporary redirect to a raw URL
Permanent redirect to a raw URL
Redirect to another action in the same controller

data.text: You cannot pass a model object through `RedirectToAction`. Use TempData or session if you need to carry data across the redirect.
Returning JSON and Status Codes
Action methods are not limited to views. They can also return JSON data or plain HTTP status codes — the building blocks of a Web API.

data.expectedOutcome: You will understand how to pass data between actions using TempData and how to return views from action methods.

items.text: Action methods are public and return IActionResult or a specific result type.
items.hint: Private or protected methods are not accessible as actions.

items.text: Use ViewBag for simple, non-redirect data passing.
items.hint: ViewBag is dynamic and convenient for small amounts of data.

items.text: Use TempData when you need data to survive a single redirect.
items.hint: TempData uses session state under the hood.

items.text: Use strongly-typed models for complex data transfer.
items.hint: Models give you compile-time safety and IntelliSense.

items.text: Use RedirectToAction for navigating between actions.
items.hint: Avoid hardcoded URLs — RedirectToAction adapts if routes change.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Action methods are public methods on a controller that handle HTTP requests.
IActionResult is the most flexible return type for action methods.
Use ViewBag for simple data, TempData for redirect-safe data, and models for complex data.
RedirectToAction lets you navigate between actions without hardcoding URLs.
Actions can also return JSON or status codes for API endpoints.
data.takeaway: Action methods are the heart of every ASP.NET Core controller. Master them and you can build any kind of web response.
